title: China releases AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0
summary: The CAC website carries a notice dated 14 September 2026 that the AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0 was released at the opening of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Publicity Week. The page attributes the document to the National Cybersecurity Standardisation Technical Committee (TC260) under guidance from the CAC. It is organised around risk classification, technical response measures and comprehensive governance, and updates the risk classification and the response and governance measures relative to versions 1.0 and 2.0. The page does not state that the framework is legally binding. The Chinese page was read through a machine-translating fetch tool, so wording is paraphrased and the full framework text was not read.
why_it_matters: The framework, drafted by China's national cybersecurity standards committee under CAC guidance, sets out a classification of AI safety risks and corresponding technical and governance measures. It is not stated to create legal obligations, so its practical effect depends on how later standards and enforcement draw on it.

review.reviewer_notes: Second-round review, whole entry rechecked. Re-fetched https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-09/14/c_1791137092283345.htm on 2026-10-07 (loads; read through a translating fetch tool). Verified against the page: title 《人工智能安全治理框架3.0》发布; page date 2026-09-14; released at the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Publicity Week; released by the National Cybersecurity Standardisation Technical Committee (网安标委/TC260) under the guidance of the national cyberspace office (CAC), with CAC research and data-security centres and other institutions involved in drafting; keeps the core logic of risk classification, technical response and comprehensive governance; updates the risk classification and optimises the technical and governance measures relative to 1.0 (2024) and 2.0 (2025). The page has no statement on binding force and no effective date, so 'does not state that the framework is legally binding' is accurate. Every sentence in summary is supported. why_it_matters: first sentence now matches the round-1 wording and is supported. The second sentence ('practical effect depends on how later standards and enforcement draw on it') is a conditional inference, not a prediction stated as fact, and is framed as a consequence of the non-binding status; acceptable. event_date 2026-09-14 is the release date and matches the page (no separate adoption or effective date exists on the page). Stage in_force is the closest STAGES value for a released non-binding document; type guidance is consistent with a TC260 document. Source tier primary is correct (CAC is the guiding body and the publisher of the notice). Confidence was lowered to low as required in round 1, consistent with the rubric for machine-translated sources, and the summary explains why. Duplicate check: grep of content/items, content/instruments and content/digests (excluding runs) for 'safety governance', 'governance framework', 'TC260' and the source URL found only the unrelated Singapore agentic AI framework; existing China instruments are the labelling measures, cybersecurity law amendment and generative AI interim measures. Only one item in this file for the event. Round-1 required changes both applied. Minor, not blocking: accessed_at 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z looks like a placeholder midnight time rather than the actual fetch time.
